subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation expectations
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@finsecure.com>, Jacob Lee <jacob.lee@finsecure.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation expectations

Hi Alice / Jacob —

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the deployment constraints you mentioned:

1) Primary concern: strict data isolation for model inputs/outputs and inference logs. You called out regulatory requirements that preclude any co-mingled customer workloads on the same GPU hosts.
2) Key controls you want to confirm:
   - Customer-managed KMS (HSM or CMKs) for all data-at-rest encryption
   - Audit logs and full access to request traces (retention policy to be determined)
   - Network isolation: VPC peering or PrivateLink; no public egress from inference hosts without customer control

From our side, the two deployment options that meet this bar (depending on your operational preferences) are:
- Redwood Dedicated: reserved GPU pools that are single-tenant for your org, with options for network controls and KMS integration. Lower ops overhead since we manage the hardware but guarantees around multi-tenancy depend on contract and placement.
- Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem): customer-managed networking and optional on-prem deployment; gives you the highest degree of isolation (you control the subnet, egress, and keys).

A few follow-ups we need to decide with you:
- Do you require customer-controlled physical hosts (on-prem) or is logical separation (Dedicated single-tenant by customer) sufficient?
- KMS: will your security team require an on-prem HSM, or is cloud KMS with customer-managed keys acceptable?
- Audit log retention window and location (S3 bucket in customer account vs. Redwood-managed storage)

I attached a short slide deck that summarizes the two options and a SOC2 summary per your request.

Proposed next step: technical deep-dive with Rishi (Solutions Architect) — 60 minutes to go over KMS integration, network controls, and audit/export requirements. Are you available for a walkthrough next week? 

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142

From: Alice Nguyen <alice@finsecure.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jacob Lee <jacob.lee@finsecure.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation expectations

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and the slides — helpful. A few clarifications from our side after syncing with security/legal: 

- Our regulators require that production inference never run on shared multi-tenant GPUs where another customer could access the same physical host. So "single-tenant" dedicated by logical controls is only acceptable if you can guarantee physical isolation (i.e., dedicated hosts pinned to our account).
- Audit logs must be exportable to our S3 (in our AWS account) and retained for a minimum of 7 years.
- KMS: we plan to require customer-controlled keys. Cloud KMS with CMKs in our AWS account is acceptable; on-prem HSM would be ideal but not strictly required if CMKs meet the attestation bar.
- Network: no public egress by default; any egress must go through our approved transit gateway.

Given this, we're leaning toward Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) as the safest long-term approach; however, if Dedicated can provide physically isolated hosts, with KMS in our account and S3 log export, it could be a near-term option.

Can Rishi confirm whether Dedicated supports host pinning and full S3 export + CMK integration? Also please share any SOC2 artifacts you have (I saw the SOC2 summary in the deck but our auditors typically want the control matrix).

Best,
Alice Nguyen
VP, Security & Compliance
FinSecure
alice@finsecure.com | (617) 555-0198

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@finsecure.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jacob Lee <jacob.lee@finsecure.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation expectations

Hi Alice — thanks for the detail, that helps. Quick technical answers and clarifications from the Redwood side: 

1) Dedicated (reserved capacity): we can offer host pinning in many of our Dedicated offerings — that means GPUs/hosts are physically isolated and allocated only to your account. This is dependent on capacity and will be part of the Dedicated contract (we'll flag as a SLA-able deliverable).

2) KMS/Encryption: we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) in your AWS account for all data-at-rest. For customers needing HSM-backed keys we offer integration patterns; depending on the HSM vendor we can operate in a hybrid setup (on-prem HSM or cloud HSM with attestation).

3) Audit logs / retention: we can export inference logs and audit trails to an S3 bucket in your account. Retention policies are configurable; 7+ years is feasible but will impact storage/ingress costs — we can model that for the deal.

4) Network controls: PrivateLink or VPC peering is supported; we can ensure no public egress from inference hosts. For Private (VPC/on-prem) you get the tightest controls since the control plane can be customer-managed.

Next steps I recommend:
- Technical deep-dive (60 min) to validate the host pinning flow, KMS key rotation/process, and S3 export pipeline. I can run through a sample architecture and timelines.
- Security artifacts: I'll attach our control matrix and SOC2 attest once I confirm the latest package from our compliance team (should be ready this afternoon).

If you'd like, we can also provide a short TCO/ops comparison for Dedicated vs Private for your infra team to review.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
